verses.text: “Brothers and fathers, listen to me as I make my defense.”
When they heard him speaking in Hebrew, they became even quieter. He continued,

“I’m a Jew, born in Tarsus in Cilicia, but raised right here in this city. I studied at Gamaliel’s feet and was trained carefully in the Law of our ancestors. I was just as passionate for God as all of you are today.
“I persecuted the Way all the way to death. I arrested and imprisoned both men and women.

“The high priest and the whole council of elders can confirm this. They gave me letters for our fellow Jews, and I traveled to Damascus to arrest the believers there and bring them back to Jerusalem for punishment.
“About noon, as I was traveling and getting close to Damascus, a bright light from heaven suddenly flashed all around me.
“I fell to the ground and heard a voice say, ‘Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting me?’
“I answered, ‘Who are you, Lord?’ He said to me, ‘I am Jesus of Nazareth, the one you are persecuting.’
“The people traveling with me saw the light, but they didn’t understand the voice speaking to me. They were afraid.
“I asked, ‘What should I do, Lord?’ The Lord said, ‘Get up and go to Damascus. There you’ll be told everything I’ve appointed you to do.’
“The light was so bright that I couldn’t see. My companions led me by the hand into Damascus.
“There was a devout man named Ananias who lived by the Law and was respected by all the Jews in Damascus.
“He came and stood beside me. ‘Brother Saul, receive your sight!’ he said. At that very moment, I could see him.
“Then he said, ‘The God of our ancestors chose you to know his will, to see the Righteous One, and to hear him speak.
“You’ll be his witness to everyone, telling them what you’ve seen and heard.
“So what are you waiting for? Get up, be baptized, and wash away your sins as you call on the Lord’s name.’
“Later, when I had returned to Jerusalem and was praying in the temple, I fell into a trance
and saw the Lord saying to me, ‘Hurry! Leave Jerusalem right away, because they won’t accept your testimony about me.’
“I said, ‘Lord, they know I went from synagogue to synagogue arresting and beating those who believed in you.
“When the blood of Stephen, your witness, was spilled, I stood there agreeing with it. I even guarded the coats of the people who killed him.’
“But the Lord said to me, ‘Go! I’m sending you far away to the Gentiles.’”
The crowd listened until Paul said that. Then they shouted, “Get rid of this man! He doesn’t deserve to live!”
As they yelled, threw off their coats, and tossed dust into the air,
the commander ordered Paul taken into the barracks. He told the soldiers to question him by whipping him so he could find out why the crowd was shouting like this.
As they stretched Paul out to whip him, he asked the nearby centurion, “Is it legal for you to whip a Roman citizen who hasn’t been found guilty?”
When the centurion heard that, he went to the commander and warned him, “Be careful what you’re about to do. This man is a Roman citizen!”
The commander came and asked Paul, “Tell me, are you a Roman citizen?” “Yes,” Paul answered.
The commander said, “I paid a lot of money for my citizenship.” Paul replied, “I was born a citizen.”
Right away, the men who were about to question Paul backed off. The commander was alarmed too, because he had ordered a Roman citizen chained up.

The next day, wanting to find out exactly why the Jews accused Paul, the commander released him from his chains. He ordered the chief priests and the whole council to meet, then brought Paul down and stood him before them.
